title: Adding PLDM dissector for FRU Specification
description:
This commit implemements PLDM dissector
for the FRU specification of the protocol
which is done following DMTF guideline
documentation -
https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0257_1.0.0.pdf

Testing : For verification of dissector
pcap file collected during host poweron
is used as well as used custom pcaps.

Signed-off-by: Riya Dixit <riyadixitagra@gmail.com>

I can't work out what is going here.  There are always 8 bytes, and i represents which byte we are looking at?
correct, the last 8 bytes will have bits set corresponding to PLDM type that is supported in a particular PLDM version. 'i' here is each byte in 8bytes and 'j' here is for bits in a byte.

changed this line in [version 8 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14225/diffs?diff_id=925681987&start_sha=21d6deed05204842c4c68b1053e41dc0af3305c7#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_612_593)

type is the current byte?
Correct, the current type from the 8 bytes which are being checked if they have bit set. For details -https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0240_1.0.0.pdf Table 11.

changed this line in [version 8 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14225/diffs?diff_id=925681987&start_sha=21d6deed05204842c4c68b1053e41dc0af3305c7#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_613_593)
so supported_type is the bit position between 0 and 63 (but bit positions within a byte are 'backwards') ?
correct but backwards because of endianness of the protocol

changed this line in [version 8 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14225/diffs?diff_id=925681987&start_sha=21d6deed05204842c4c68b1053e41dc0af3305c7#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_617_593)

so you show the enums associated with that byte while selecting that byte?  This would at least be less confusing if you show the value as decimal rather than hex (as that is what is in your value_string).

I'd still be tempted to show it as a single call to add_bitmask() - where the items could use something like

FT_BOOLEAN, 64, TFS(&tfs_present_not_present)

and avoid the confusing nest loop.  What you would lose is showing the number of the supported type - I don't know if this matters to you.

the purpose of this command is to show all the supported commands of that particular PLDM type based on the set bits we receive.... did I make sense or is there something else you are asking and I didn't catch it?
I think adding separate bool items (as above) for each flag, then calling proto_tree_add_bitmask() with the set would show this more nicely.  It was also show the user which flags were not set.
I wanted to keep the logic similar to the way its documented for various reasons. It maybe a minor overhead, if it's okay to keep it this way, it will be better for PLDM community I think.

At least add a comment to say that its effectively 8 bytes of bit flags, and maybe choose some less confusing variable names?  add_bitmask() would make it much easier to understand (i.e. which bit corresponds to which flag), and avoids worrying nested loops.
sure, I will add comments and change variable name.
Done
I had to manually set this... not sure we should be trying to claim dynamic/unclaimed DLTs
I am not aware about this, I did not face this myself. Is there some other way to do this ?

These dynamic DLTs should not be assigned (by default) to any dissector.  If there is no encapsulation for these frames, you can use one of these dynamic ones, or if appropriate consider proposing a new encapsulation (https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes.html)
On wire, we will never receive PLDM frames, it is always payload to a transport protocol as of now MCTP so we can continue this way.
So delete this line then!  You can't try to claim the first dynamic link type in your dissector.

changed this line in [version 8 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14225/diffs?diff_id=925681987&start_sha=21d6deed05204842c4c68b1053e41dc0af3305c7#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_1849_1783)
Done
What is this line trying to accomplish?

As PLDM is a application layer protocol so we receive it as MCTP packet payload. MCTP has various msg_types one of them is PLDM - https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0239_1.3.0.pdf : Table 1. If we collect  pcaps from the processor, we get MCTP pcaps inside which we have PLDM packets.
